### What is chikungunya and how does it spread?

Chikungunya disease is caused by the chikungunya virus. It's spread through infected Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. People can get sick within 3 to 7 days of a bite from a mosquito carrying the virus.

# Chikungunya in Argentina: Salta is the epicenter

Robert Herriman

In a follow-up on the chikungunya outbreak in Argentina, health authorities report a total of 433 chikungunya cases—357 are autochthonous, while only 76 have a history of travel (imported cases) to Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Cuba.

Photo by National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases on Unsplash

Salta is the epicenter of the outbreak with 315 cases. [...] The localities with the most cases are Salvador Mazza (189 cases), Aguas Blancas (34 cases), Embarcación (20 cases), and San Ramón de la Nueva Orán (20 cases).

According to the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), Argentina has reported the third most confirmed chikungunya cases in the Americas, following only Brazil, Suriname and Bolivia.

Chikungunya epidemic risk: A call to action [...] Chikungunya is a viral disease transmitted by the bite of infected mosquitoes such as Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus. It can cause high fever, joint pain, muscle pain, and headache. Although chikungunya disease rarely causes death, the joint pain associated with the disease can last for months or years and can become a cause of chronic pain and disability.

snippet: # New York health officials confirm state’s first locally acquired case of chikungunya virus A person living in New York tested positive for the mosquito-borne chikungunya virus in the first reported transmission within the US in six years, officials said on Tuesday. The chikungunya virus is currently running rampant through China and other nearby countries, the New York Department of Health said. It’s not clear how the person contracted the virus, but health officials said that they were most likely bitten by an infected mosquito. Three other instances of the virus were recorded in the country earlier this year, but all the cases could be traced back to international travel through regions where chikungunya is prevalent, state health officials said.

title: US issues travel warning to China: ‘Enhanced precautions’ urged amid disease spread; Beijing revives COVI - Times of India
snippet: US health officials have raised a travel alert for China’s Guangdong province after a surge in cases of chikungunya, a mosquito-borne illness known to cause prolonged joint pain.According to the New York Post, the center for disease control and prevention (CDC) has issued a Level 2 travel warning, advising visitors to “practice enhanced precautions” when visiting the region. Two vaccines against chikungunya have recently been approved for use in the United States, but pregnant women - particularly those nearing delivery - are advised to reconsider travel as the virus can, in rare cases, be transmitted during childbirth.Globally, an estimated 35 million people contract chikungunya each year, though annual deaths are relatively low at around 3,700.
